translation_en: Abu al-Yaman informed us; Shuayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The womb is a bond from the Most Merciful. Allah said: Whoever maintains ties with you, I will maintain ties with him; and whoever severs you, I will sever ties with him.”

Abdullah ibn Yusuf informed us; Malik informed us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-Araj, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most false kind of speech. Do not seek out people's faults, do not spy, do not outbid one another to inflate prices, do not envy one another, do not hate one another, do not turn away from one another, and be servants of Allah as brothers.”

Said ibn Ufair narrated to us; al-Layth narrated to us, from Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from Urwah, from Aishah, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “I do not think so-and-so and so-and-so know anything of our religion.” Al-Layth said: They were two hypocritical men.

Abd al-Aziz ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Ibrahim ibn Sad narrated to us, from his nephew Ibn Shihab, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim ibn Abdullah, who said: I heard Abu Hurairah say: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: “All of my community may be pardoned except those who openly publicize their sins. It is part of shamelessness for a man to do something at night, then in the morning—after Allah had concealed it—to say, ‘So-and-so, I did such-and-such last night,’ when his Lord had concealed him during the night and he reveals Allah's concealment in the morning.”

Muhammad ibn Kathir informed us; Sufyan informed us; Mabid ibn Khalid al-Qaysi narrated to us, from Harithah ibn Wahb al-Khuzai, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “Shall I tell you who the people of Paradise are? Every humble, unassuming person who, if he swore by Allah, Allah would fulfill his oath. Shall I tell you who the people of the Fire are? Every harsh, arrogant, and conceited person.”

Abdullah ibn Yusuf informed us; Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Do not hate one another, do not envy one another, do not turn away from one another, and be servants of Allah as brothers. It is not lawful for a Muslim to abandon his brother for more than three nights.”

Abdullah ibn Yusuf informed us; Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Ata ibn Yazid al-Laythi, from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “It is not lawful for a man to abandon his brother for more than three nights: they meet, and each turns away from the other. The better of the two is the one who begins with the greeting of peace.”

Musaddad narrated to us; Yahya narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas, who said: When Abd al-Rahman arrived among us, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, established brotherhood between him and Sad ibn al-Rabi. The Prophet said: “Hold a wedding feast, even if only with one sheep.”

Muhammad ibn Sabah narrated to us; Ismail ibn Zakariyya narrated to us; Asim narrated to us, saying: I asked Anas ibn Malik: “Did you hear that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, ‘There is no alliance in Islam’?” He said: “The Prophet established an alliance between Quraysh and the Ansar in my house.”

Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us; Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Wail, from Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “Truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. A man continues to tell the truth until he is recorded with Allah as thoroughly truthful. Lying leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire. A man continues to lie until he is recorded with Allah as a liar.”

Ibn Salam narrated to us; Ismail ibn Jafar narrated to us, from Abu Suhayl Nafi ibn Malik ibn Abi Amir, from his father, from Abu Hurairah, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The signs of a hypocrite are three: when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks it; and when entrusted, he betrays the trust.”

Musa ibn Ismail narrated to us; Jarir narrated to us; Abu Raja narrated to us, from Samurah ibn Jundub, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “I saw two men come to me. They said: The man whose cheek you saw being torn apart was a liar who told a lie that was carried from him until it reached the horizons; that will be done to him until the Day of Resurrection.”

Musaddad narrated to us; Yahya ibn Said narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: Al-Amash narrated to me, from Said ibn Jubayr, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “No one—or nothing—is more patient with hurtful things he hears than Allah. They ascribe a child to Him, yet He still grants them well-being and provides for them.”

Muhammad and Ahmad ibn Said narrated to us; they said: Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us; Ali ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “If a man says to his brother, ‘O disbeliever,’ then the charge falls back upon one of them.” Ikrimah ibn Ammar also reported from Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Yazid, who heard Abu Salamah, who heard Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet.

Ismail narrated to us: Malik narrated to me, from Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “If any man says to his brother, ‘O disbeliever,’ then the charge falls back upon one of them.”

Musa ibn Ismail narrated to us; Wuhayb narrated to us; Ayyub narrated to us, from Abu Qilabah, from Thabit ibn al-Dahhak, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “Whoever falsely swears by a religion other than Islam is as he said. Whoever kills himself with something will be punished with it in the Fire of Hell. Cursing a believer is like killing him, and whoever accuses a believer of disbelief is like one who kills him.”

Muhammad ibn Abadah informed us; Yazid informed us; Sulaym informed us; Amr ibn Dinar narrated to us; Jabir ibn Abdullah narrated to us: Muadh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, used to pray with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, then return to his people and lead them in prayer. He recited al-Baqarah for them. A man shortened his prayer and prayed briefly. When Muadh heard of this, he said: “He is a hypocrite.” The man heard about it and came to the Prophet, saying: “Messenger of Allah, we work with our hands and irrigate with our camels. Muadh led us in prayer last night and recited al-Baqarah, so I shortened my prayer, and he claims I am a hypocrite.” The Prophet said: “Muadh, are you causing people hardship?” He repeated it three times. “Recite ‘By the sun and its morning brightness’ (Quran 91:1), ‘Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High’ (Quran 87:1), and similar short chapters.”

Ishaq narrated to me; Abu al-Mughirah informed us; al-Awzai narrated to us; al-Zuhri narrated to us, from Humayd, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “If one of you swears by al-Lat and al-Uzza, let him say: ‘There is no god but Allah.’ And whoever says to his companion, ‘Come, let us gamble,’ let him give charity.”

Yasrah ibn Safwan narrated to us; Ibrahim narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from al-Qasim, from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, entered while there was a curtain in the house bearing images. His face changed color, then he took the curtain and tore it. She said: The Prophet said: “Among the people who will suffer the severest punishment on the Day of Resurrection are those who make these images.”

Al-Makki said: Abdullah ibn Said narrated to us. Muhammad ibn Ziyad narrated to me; Muhammad ibn Jafar narrated to us; Abdullah ibn Said narrated to us, saying: Salim Abu al-Nadr, the freedman of Umar ibn Ubaydullah, narrated to me, from Busr ibn Said, from Zayd ibn Thabit, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, set aside a small enclosed space made with woven palm branches or a mat. He went out and prayed there, and men followed him and prayed along with him. One night they came and waited, but the Messenger of Allah was delayed and did not come out to them. They raised their voices and threw pebbles at the door. He came out to them angrily and said: “You kept doing this until I thought it might be made obligatory for you. Pray in your homes, for a man's best prayer is in his home, except for the prescribed prayer.”

Abdullah ibn Yusuf informed us; Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Said ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The strong person is not the one who defeats others in wrestling; rather, the strong person is the one who controls himself when angry.”

Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us; Jarir narrated to us, from al-Amash, from Adi ibn Thabit. Sulayman ibn Surad narrated to us, who said: Two men insulted one another in the presence of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, while we were sitting with him. One of them was insulting his companion in anger, and his face had become red. The Prophet said: “I know a phrase which, if he said it, would make what he is feeling go away: ‘I seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the accursed.’” They said to the man: “Do you not hear what the Prophet is saying?” He replied: “I am not mad.”

Adam narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu al-Sawwar al-Adawi, who said: I heard Imran ibn Husayn say: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Modesty brings nothing but good.” Bashir ibn Kab said: It is written in wisdom: “Modesty brings dignity, and modesty brings tranquility.” Imran said to him: “I am narrating to you from the Messenger of Allah, and you are telling me from your book?”

Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us; Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Salamah narrated to us; Ibn Shihab narrated to us, from Salim, from Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by a man who was being admonished for his modesty. He was told: “You are so modest,” as though it were harming him. The Messenger of Allah said: “Leave him, for modesty is part of faith.”

Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us; Zuhayr narrated to us; Mansur narrated to us; Rabii ibn Hirash narrated to us; Abu Masud narrated to us, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Among the words of the earliest prophethood that people have retained is: If you feel no shame, then do as you wish.”

Adam narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu al-Tayyah, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, say: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Make things easy and do not make them difficult; bring calm and do not drive people away.”

Abu al-Yaman informed us; Shuayb informed us, from al-Zuhri. Al-Layth also said: Yunus narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah informed me that Abu Hurairah told him: A Bedouin urinated in the mosque, and the people rushed to stop him. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to them: “Leave him, and pour a bucket—or a large container—of water over his urine. You have been sent to make things easy, not to make them difficult.”

Qutaybah narrated to us; al-Layth narrated to us, from Uqayl, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “A believer is not stung from the same hole twice.”

Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us; Ibn Mahdi narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should not harm his neighbor. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honor his guest. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent.”

Qutaybah narrated to us; al-Layth narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu al-Khayr, from Uqbah ibn Amir, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: We said: “Messenger of Allah, you send us out and we stay with people who do not host us. What do you advise?” The Messenger of Allah said: “If you stay with people and they provide what is appropriate for a guest, accept it. If they do not, take from them the guest's due that is appropriate for them to provide.”
